children: New Delhi, Oct. 20 -- The US and India are "very, very close" to a trade agreement, with only a small number of items yet to be decided upon, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said on Tuesday, exuding optimism that the pact would be in place very soon.

"We're very, very close. I would say we're about as close as you can be without having executed the agreement," Rubio told the press in Mumbai. "I think there's a small number of items to wrap up, so I think that will happen shortly - we're hoping; it should."
"Obviously the state department doesn't negotiate trade agreements, but we are very much involved in what's happening," he said.

Rubio described India as an important commercial and business partner of the US, referring to bilateral defence cooperation and India's membership of the Quad, a strategic partnership between India, the US, Japan and Australia, focusing on security, technology and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"This is the most populous country in the world; it's the largest democracy in the world. It's an important commercial partner and business partner of the United States. We also do a lot of defence cooperation. They're a key member of the Quad. They're a strong strategic partner," he said.

In FY26, India's exports to the US grew marginally to $87.31 billion from $86.51 billion a year ago, while imports surged by 17.2% to $53.45 billion from $45.62 billion in FY25. Overall bilateral trade rose 6.5% to $140.76 billion in FY26 from $132.2 billion. India had a trade surplus of $33.9 billion in FY26, down from $40.9 billion in FY25.
Rubio said trade was one of two subjects that featured in his conversations with counterparts around the world, the other being demand for air interceptors.

The top US official's visit to India is scheduled to run until 22 October, according to the external affairs ministry. His itinerary includes engagements in Mumbai and a visit to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Wednesday, where he is slated to discuss energy cooperation with entities including Reliance Industries Ltd that operates the world's largest single-site oil refining complex in Jamnagar.
In Mumbai, Rubio spoke about India's refining capabilities and the potential role of Venezuelan crude oil, and said he would discuss the issue with Reliance in Jamnagar on Wednesday.

"They can, and we'll talk about that tomorrow with Reliance... They have the capability to refine heavy crude. They've done so in the past, and I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do," Rubio said.

". India is a refining superpower, and they have the ability to do that. They have companies that know how to do that," he added. Indian companies had oil concessions in Venezuela and could produce more themselves, he said.

"I'm not claiming to you that Venezuela alone can fill the hole that could be caused by some of the things that are happening around the world, but I think over time it most certainly can. And in the short term, it can somewhat provide relief," he said alluding to the energy shortages due to disruptions caused by the ongoing West Asia war.
Rubio said sanctions could pose impediments that would need to be addressed.
Rubio said India had expressed a desire to diversify its energy portfolio, and that the major importing nation had made progress in this regard.

"I think what India has expressed repeatedly is their desire to diversify their energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do. Obviously, it's not easy to do that from one day to the next. So, I think they've made substantial progress in that regard, and we're happy to see that," he said. "But in the end, it's not just about Russian oil, it's about their desire to diversify."

title: US, India 'very, very close' to trade deal, says Rubio
